summary: The plan-doc carries four MAJ-class safety gaps: (1) the invocation-log gate (invariant 2) is pure policy with no enforcement mechanism, meaning a cascade slice can declare an adopter onboarded without the log entry ever being committed; (2) the enable-required-check.sh script hardcodes the WP-SCP-020 log path, so every WP-SCP-024 cascade invocation emits instructions pointing the operator to the wrong file; (3) the --restore rollback mode (invariant 7 SLO <30 min) does not exist at plan-doc merge time and §10 Q9 openly acknowledges its test surface is unsolved, making the SLO aspirational at the moment when cascade slices start invoking the forward-mode of the script; (4) invariant 8's Renovate-cycle-clean check is waivable via the R-024-07 fallback, meaning an adopter with Renovate disabled can be declared onboarded without proof that automated version-skew tolerance works. Two additional MIN-class findings cover the FLA-learning propagation gap and the T-024-10 conflict-deferral ambiguity.

findings.title: Invocation-log gate (invariant 2) is policy-only — no enforcement mechanism prevents a cascade slice from declaring onboarding without the log entry committed
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-024-estate-cascade.md §2 invariant 2: 'An apply without the log entry is unrecorded. Cascade slices that fail to commit the invocation log are blocked from declaring the adopter onboarded.' The blocking mechanism is unstated. §5.2 says the SCP-side cascade slice PR ships the invocation-log entry — but this is the same PR that the orchestrator merges; nothing in the CI pipeline checks that `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-024/branch-protection-log.md` was modified in the PR, or that the entry's target repo matches the slice's DISPATCH-NOTE target. The plan-doc also defers ratification of invariant 2 'in code form' to 024B via D-044 (§9 D-044 row: 'Ratifies invariants 2 + 3 + 10 in code form') — meaning at 024A merge there is no code-enforced check.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI step (e.g. a shell script checked into `scripts/check-invocation-log-entry.sh`) that asserts: (a) `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-024/branch-protection-log.md` was modified in the PR diff, and (b) the modified entry contains the target repo string extracted from the DISPATCH-NOTE. Gate 024B's D-044 on this CI step existing — do not allow 024C (first cascade slice against a real adopter repo) to open until the enforcement mechanism is committed. The plan-doc must name this CI check as a hard predecessor for 024C, not just a D-044 deliverable aspiration.

findings.title: enable-required-check.sh hardcodes the WP-SCP-020 log path — every cascade invocation emits instructions directing the operator to the wrong log file
findings.evidence: scripts/enable-required-check.sh line 436: `LOG_FILE="docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md"`. The emitted log block (lines 443–476) instructs the operator: 'Append the block below to ${LOG_FILE} on the SCP repo'. The plan-doc requires entries in `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-024/branch-protection-log.md` (§5.2 point 2, §3, and §8 Threshold A criteria row 2: 'Each onboarded adopter has a corresponding entry in `docs/reviews/WP-SCP-024/branch-protection-log.md`'). A cascade operator following the script's emitted instructions will paste the entry into the WP-SCP-020 log, leaving the WP-SCP-024 log absent. The Threshold A criterion requiring per-adopter entries in the WP-SCP-024 log will then appear unsatisfied even after successful onboarding.
findings.recommendation: Before 024C opens, add a `--log-file` argument to `enable-required-check.sh` (defaulting to the existing WP-SCP-020 path for backward compatibility) so cascade invocations can pass `--log-file docs/reviews/WP-SCP-024/branch-protection-log.md` explicitly. Document the required argument in the §5.4 extension spec and in the D-044 ratification row. Alternatively, teach the script to accept a `SCP_LOG_FILE` env var and set it in each cascade slice's DISPATCH-NOTE invocation block. The fix must land in 024B before any cascade slice runs the script against a real adopter repo.

findings.title: Per-adopter rollback (invariant 7, SLO <30 min) is aspirational at plan-doc merge — the --restore mode does not exist and its test surface is an open question
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-024-estate-cascade.md §2 invariant 7: 'enable-required-check.sh --restore <pre-state>.json reverts branch protection to the captured before-state ... Rollback time SLO: <30 minutes from operator decision to merge-restored state.' §5.4 states the --restore mode 'added at slice 024B.' §10 Q9: 'the rollback mode lands at 024B. How is it tested without actually mutating an estate repo? Open at 024B; likely a fixture-based dry-run mode ... before any cohort adopter cascade.' §6 slice plan: 024B acceptance criterion for the --restore mode is 'round-trip via captured before-state restores branch-protection state byte-for-byte' — a reasonable criterion but one whose implementation is explicitly unknown at 024A. The plan-doc does not require 024B to close Q9 before 024C opens; the sequencing note only says '024B is a hard predecessor for 024C–024F' without specifying that --restore must be demonstrated functional (not merely merged) before 024C.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit acceptance criterion to slice 024B: '--restore mode must be demonstrated functional via a real-repo round-trip on a throw-away test repo (not just a dry-run mock) before 024C opens.' Amend the plan-doc §5.4 to state: 'The --restore mode is a hard prerequisite for 024C; the <30-min rollback SLO is not claimed until 024B closes with a demonstrated round-trip.' This makes the SLO honest at 024A merge time. Additionally, add a §10 Q9 resolution path: Q9 is closed (not left open) only when 024B acceptance criterion explicitly includes the throw-away-repo round-trip test.

findings.title: Invariant 8 Renovate-cycle-clean check is waivable for adopters with Renovate disabled — an adopter without Renovate can be declared onboarded without proof of automated version-skew tolerance
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-024-estate-cascade.md §2 invariant 8: 'A cascade slice that completes onboarding without a version-bump occurring during bake MUST extend bake until at least one Renovate-issued SHA pin bump has been merged + observed clean.' T-024-07 closure criterion: 'Renovate PR # (merged): ___, observed-clean date: ___' and 'refuse to declare onboarding without both fields populated.' R-024-07 mitigation: 'without Renovate, the post-bake window is satisfied by an operator-driven SHA pin bump PR instead.' The R-024-07 mitigation explicitly allows an operator-driven SHA pin bump to satisfy both fields — meaning a cascade slice can populate 'Renovate PR # (merged): N/A (operator-driven)' and declare onboarding clean. An adopter whose Renovate is non-functional will then be declared onboarded without any evidence that automated version-skew tolerance works, which is the explicit purpose of the bake window per invariant 8. The Threshold A criterion in §8 requires '≥1 SCP minor version-bump cycle has propagated cleanly to those adopters via Renovate' but the per-adopter R-024-07 mitigation contradicts this by allowing non-Renovate propagation.
findings.recommendation: Tighten R-024-07: the operator-driven bump is acceptable as a temporary unblock, but it must be accompanied by a forward-filed TF to fix Renovate on that adopter before the adopter counts toward Threshold A. Amend §8 Threshold A: '≥1 SCP minor version-bump cycle has propagated cleanly to those adopters — via Renovate OR via operator-driven bump with a filed TF requiring Renovate to be enabled before the adopter's Threshold-A contribution is credited.' This distinguishes adopters that genuinely exercise automated version-skew tolerance from those that satisfy the letter of the criterion via a one-off operator action.

findings.title: FLA-independent invariant 4 creates a silent safety gap — no mechanism ensures FLA pilot safety discoveries propagate to non-FLA cascade slices
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-024-estate-cascade.md §2 invariant 4: 'cascade slices may opportunistically reference FLA learnings but MUST NOT add any FLA precondition.' §1 predecessor block: 'WP-SCP-020.1 (FLA pilot) — separate track, not a predecessor for this WP.' The FLA pilot is the first real-world test of the federation primitive on a non-SCP repo; it may surface wrapper configuration surprises (e.g., permission footprint on a different org, OIDC behaviour differences, fork-PR if: guard edge cases). Invariant 4 explicitly prohibits adding FLA preconditions but does not establish any channel for safety-relevant FLA findings to be tracked as cascade-slice checklist items. The plan-doc provides no mechanism for 'opportunistic reference' — no FLA safety-lessons registry, no checkpoint in each cascade slice's DISPATCH-NOTE requiring the reviewer to confirm 'no new FLA safety findings since last slice.'
findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight FLA-safety-lessons checkpoint to each cascade slice's DISPATCH-NOTE template (to be specified in D-044): a single line 'FLA pilot safety findings reviewed: [none new / <link to finding>]' that the cascade slice author populates. This is not a FLA precondition — it is a check that the author has looked at the FLA pilot state before opening the cascade slice, so safety discoveries don't silently accumulate between slices. Amend §5.2 per-adopter onboarding contract to include this checkpoint as item (5).

findings.title: T-024-10 conflict-handling path is internally inconsistent — 'cascade defers' and 'cascade notes the conflict; it does not fix it' are different outcomes with no specified closure path
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-024-estate-cascade.md §4 T-024-10 mitigation: 'If the adopter has a pre-existing `policy-check` workflow, the cascade slice DEFERS until the adopter's existing workflow is renamed (per invariant 10: forward-filed TF, not blocked by cascade).' Invariant 10: 'if discovered necessary during cascade (e.g. adopter has a stale `policy-check.yml` from a prior unrelated experiment), that's filed as a forward TF and unblocks the cascade slice via documenting the conflict, not via fixing it.' R-024-06 mitigation: 'cascade defers; forward-files TF; does not modify adopter content per invariant 10.' T-024-10 says the cascade slice 'DEFERS until the adopter's existing workflow is renamed' (implying the cascade slice stays open pending the rename) while invariant 10 says the slice 'unblocks' by documenting (implying the slice closes without onboarding). These are different resolution states. Neither specifies: who renames the adopter's workflow, on what timeline, and whether the cascade slice is reverted on the SCP side or merely annotated as 'conflict-pending.'
findings.recommendation: Resolve the T-024-10 / invariant 10 inconsistency in the plan-doc: specify that when a workflow name conflict is discovered, (a) the cascade slice CLOSES on the SCP side with status 'blocked-on-adopter-conflict' rather than deferring indefinitely, (b) the forward-filed TF is owned by the cascade slice author and targets the adopter-side rename, and (c) a new cascade sub-slice opens when the conflict is resolved. This eliminates the open-ended 'defer' state that could leave the cascade slice in limbo. Amend T-024-10 and invariant 10 to use consistent terminology.
